I've been farming these 6 mu for 30 years. Same as last year, I plant wheat after maize — that's how it goes here in Quzhou. Everyone does wheat-maize.

For wheat, I use the same hybrid seed my neighbor Old Wang uses — Jimai type, it grew well last year, around 500 kg per mu. I buy two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base fertilizer before planting, that's about 50 kg. Then at jointing in spring I top-dress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. Total nitrogen comes to around 14-15 kg per mu. I plough the field before wheat — the soil needs turning after maize.

Irrigation: wheat needs water at least 3 times — winter water, jointing, and grain filling. I have the well so this is fine, just the electricity cost. Sometimes 4 times if spring is dry.

Pesticide: wheat needs spraying for aphids and powdery mildew, usually 2 times. I also spray herbicide once in spring.

For maize in summer, I plant right after wheat harvest — no time to waste. Rotary tillage only, or sometimes direct seeding without tilling. Denghai or Zhengdan hybrid seed, neighbors get 550-600 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer at planting, maybe 40 kg per mu, then urea at big trumpet stage, 20 kg. Maize eats more nitrogen than wheat.

Maize irrigation 2 times usually — at jointing and tasseling if no rain. Pesticide twice for corn borer and armyworm.

I don't want to cut fertilizer — if I save 50 yuan and lose 50 kg grain, that's stupid. Better put enough on.
